root_cause.mechanism: When evaluating markers, if the environment key is 'extra', the values are passed to `canonicalize_name`. If the environment passes `None` for `extra`, `canonicalize_name` raises a `TypeError` because it expects a string. This regression was introduced when PEP 685 normalization was added.

hypotheses.text: The bug is caused by `_normalize` passing `None` to `canonicalize_name` when `key == "extra"`. `canonicalize_name` expects a string and fails. Handling `None` in `_normalize` should fix it.
hypotheses.predicts: If I modify `src/packaging/markers.py` to handle `None` in `_normalize`, the reproduction script will print `False` instead of raising `TypeError`.
hypotheses.evidence: Applying the fix to handle None in _normalize resolved the TypeError in the reproduction script, which now prints False as expected.

hypotheses.text: The bug is caused by `Marker.evaluate` allowing `None` to be passed into the environment for `extra`. Ensuring it is converted to an empty string (or handled otherwise) before evaluation should fix it.
hypotheses.predicts: If I modify `src/packaging/markers.py` to ensure `current_environment["extra"]` is not `None` before calling `_evaluate_markers`, the reproduction script will print `False`.
hypotheses.evidence: Fixing it in _normalize worked, suggesting this was the appropriate place to handle it, as it centralizes normalization logic. While H2 might also have worked, H1 is confirmed.
